svg.aria-label: Diagram: Privileged Identity Management in Microsoft Entra, showing the four assignment combinations of permanent or time-bound against eligible or active, the fact that eligible grants identical access once activated, the gap where require multifactor authentication on activation may not prompt at all, the need for two Conditional Access policies because activation does not bind the session, and the configurable thresholds behind the PIM security alerts
svg.title: PIM does not change what an administrator can do. It changes how long, and leaves a record.
svg.text: PIM does not reduce what an admin can do. It reduces how long, and leaves a record.
Everything else follows from that: the access is identical, so the controls are all about the moment of activation and the audit trail.
Two axes, four assignments — type decides whether you act, duration decides for how long
ELIGIBLE — must activate first
ACTIVE — no action needed
PERMANENT
always able to activate
a standing administrator — what PIM exists to remove
TIME-BOUND
can activate between start and end dates
holds the role until the end date
“There’s no difference in the access given to someone with a permanent versus an eligible role assignment.
The only difference is that some people don’t need that access all the time.”
Once activated, an eligible Global Administrator is a Global Administrator. Activation is 1 to 24 hours, chosen by the user
within the maximum an administrator set. The control is the clock and the log, not the permission set.
“Require MFA on activation” may require nothing
“Users might not be prompted for multifactor
authentication if they authenticated with strong
credentials or provided multifactor authentication
earlier in the session.”
The fix is authentication context plus an authentication
strength (post #43), which forces a method different
from the one used to sign in — plus sign-in frequency
set to Every time to force it on each activation.
Even then: a 10-minute window covers later activations.
Activation does not bind the session
“After the role is activated, users aren’t prevented from
using another browsing session, device, or location to
use permissions.”
So elevate on the compliant laptop, then use the role
from anywhere. Closing it takes two policies:
1. one targeting the authentication context — what you
must satisfy to activate
2. one targeting the directory role — what you must
satisfy to use it
Four things activation does not do
Deactivate early
“You can’t deactivate a role assignment within five minutes after activation”
Revoke instantly, everywhere
an app that cached the role may still grant access after deactivation
Check the ticket number
“an information-only field. Correlation with information in any ticketing
system isn’t enforced”
Apply MFA to active assignments
PIM “can’t enforce multifactor authentication when the user uses their
role assignment because they’re already active in the role”
The configuration that locks you out of your own tenant
All three at once: every Privileged Role Administrator and Global Administrator is eligible but none active · approval is
required for activation · no approvers are configured. Nobody can activate, and nobody can approve. The documented
defence is the same one from post #41a: emergency access accounts, excluded in advance.
Alert thresholds, all configurable: unused role 0–100 days · stale account 1–365 days · Global Administrator count 2–100 and
percentage 0–100% · activation renewals 2–100 in a window you choose. Only one alert is High severity: roles assigned
outside PIM, which “might indicate an active attack”.

Sources: What is Privileged Identity Management, Configure Microsoft Entra role settings in PIM, Activate Microsoft Entra roles in PIM, and Security alerts for Microsoft Entra roles, on Microsoft Learn.
